packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-07 - unverified image-only reading (UTF-8 plain text)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this record. This is a blind reading.

LAYOUT SURVEY (from image-001.jpg, reduced overview)
- image-001.jpg shows two separate fragments on black background with a colour checker (lower left) and a cm scale (right edge).
- Left fragment: narrow vertical strip, paper (visible chain/laid lines), modern pencil shelfmark at foot "Stams, STA, Frg. 160-2r". About 18-19 lines of text in the upper two-thirds; lower third blank (end of text or blank lower margin). Single column; left edge of text cut off (line beginnings lost), right edge appears to be close to text end. Top edge torn.
- Right fragment: wider, paper, heavy damage and losses along the top (torn, irregular), with a narrow detached-looking strip on the left at top. Pencil shelfmark at foot "Stams, STA, Frg. 160-1r". About 20+ lines of dense cursive, single block; top lines partly lost to tears; brown staining in the lower middle. Text runs to the bottom edge (possibly cropped at foot).
- Script: a German-language cursive (bastarda/cursive), vernacular prose. Ink brown. No rubrics, enlarged initials, running titles or marginal glosses visible at overview scale. A small mark in the left margin of the right fragment around its 13th line.
- Language observation: vernacular German (e.g. "ich", "vnd", "die", "ding" visible at overview scale). Interpretation of genre left open.

SELECTED SPANS: whole text block of both fragments, read tile by tile.

== image-002.jpg: left fragment (Frg. 160-2r), upper part ==
Tile shows top edge (torn) and text lines 1-14 of this fragment. Left edge of text lost (first letters of each line missing); right ends of lines appear complete. Single column. Line 1 begins below a blank upper margin; a faint offset/stain above line 1 in the centre.
Abbreviations: superscript hook after d = d(er); superscript marks retained as written where unsure.

== image-008.jpg: overview of the other faces (versos) ==
- Left fragment, shelfmark "Stams, STA, Frg. 160-2v": no writing visible on this face; only show-through of the recto text, staining and laid lines. Blank face as far as the overview shows.
- Right fragment, shelfmark "Stams, STA, Frg. 160-1v": written in the same kind of brown cursive, about 22-24 lines, single block, top torn. The narrow upstanding strip is now on the right (mirror of the recto). Across the centre are several large, very dark black-letter (textura-like) characters in a vertical band, standing out from the brown text - apparently a later addition, offset, or a different layer (e.g. pasted-on or blotted text from another item); interpretation uncertain. Some lines near the foot look as if they may contain Latin words (e.g. "qui", "pro"), but that is an overview impression only. A small dark mark in the left margin about two-thirds down.
